nameStory: This cellar spider's name comes from its secretive nature - 'crypticolens' means 'hidden dweller' in Latin, referring to how it tucks itself away in dark corners and crevices. In its native Japan, it's called 'yurei-gumo' or 'ghost spider,' which perfectly captures how these pale, long-legged creatures seem to materialize from shadows in cellars and basements.
description: Pholcus crypticolens is a delicate cellar spider with extremely long, thin legs that can span several inches when extended. Like other cellar spiders, it has a small, oval body that's typically pale brown or grayish. This species is quite rare in New England, having been introduced from Japan, and builds messy, irregular webs in dark corners. When disturbed, it vibrates rapidly in its web, creating a blur of motion that makes it hard to see clearly.

idTips.label: Body Shape
idTips.description: Small, compact oval abdomen about the size of a large rice grain, attached to a thin cylindrical front section that feels delicate if accidentally touched

idTips.label: Web
idTips.description: Creates loose, irregular cobwebs in corners that feel sticky but fragile when brushed against, often accumulating dust and debris

idTips.label: Behavior
idTips.description: When threatened, vibrates so rapidly in its web that it becomes a pale blur - this 'ghost dance' is distinctive and unmistakable

idTips.label: Size
idTips.description: Leg span can reach 2-3 inches when fully extended, but body itself is tiny - less than half an inch long

idTips.label: Markings
idTips.description: Generally pale brown to grayish coloration with subtle darker markings that may be hard to see without good lighting

habitat: Found almost exclusively in human structures like basements, cellars, garages, and crawl spaces where humidity is moderate and temperatures stay relatively stable. Prefers undisturbed corners and crevices in foundations, especially areas with stone or concrete walls. Extremely rare in New England with only a couple confirmed sightings.

seasonality.spring: Adults become more active as temperatures warm, beginning to rebuild webs that may have been damaged over winter.
seasonality.summer: Peak activity period with mating and egg-laying occurring. Look for distinctive egg sacs hanging in webs during late summer.
seasonality.fall: Adults prepare for winter by seeking deeper shelter in basements and foundations. Young spiders may disperse to new locations.
seasonality.winter: Becomes less active but doesn't truly hibernate - can still be found in heated basements maintaining small webs.

funFact: This spider can live for over two years, which is exceptionally long-lived for such a delicate-looking creature - most spiders live less than one year!
confusionNotes: Easily confused with the much more common Long-bodied Cellar Spider, but crypticolens tends to be slightly smaller and paler. Memory trick: think 'cryptic coloring' for the more hidden, paler crypticolens versus the more obvious Long-bodied Cellar Spider you see everywhere.
contextualKnowledge: Despite being called a 'cellar spider,' these aren't actually closely related to true cellar spiders in some other families. The name simply refers to where they're commonly found. This species is native to Japan and very rarely encountered in New England.
compareHints: Compared to the common Long-bodied Cellar Spider, crypticolens is generally smaller and more pale in coloration. Manuel's Cellar Spider and Opilion-like Cellar Spider are even rarer in our region, but crypticolens can be distinguished by its slightly more compact body proportions and preference for deeper, more hidden locations within buildings.

relatedSpecies.distinction: Long-bodied Cellar Spiders are the most common cellar spider in New England homes and have the most extremely elongated body proportions.
Manuel's Cellar Spider is very similar to the Long-bodied Cellar Spider, and they're nearly impossible to tell apart without microscopic examination.

Distinguishing this species from its close relative, the Long-bodied Cellar Spider, requires very close examination of body proportions and leg length ratios that are difficult to assess in the field.
